primary.thesis: Access was suspended on June 12 because of a directive from the US government, not because of a bug or capacity problem that Anthropic could fix on its own. For access to come back, either the government has to withdraw or change the directive, or a court has to block it, or Anthropic has to negotiate conditions such as safeguards, audits or a staged release. Each of those runs on agency, legal or White House timelines, which usually means weeks to months, not days. The rules also set a high bar: access must be public, open to US customers and publicly announced by Anthropic. A closed beta, government-only access or access for selected enterprises does not count. The most likely way out is a partial return, such as trusted partners or a restricted API, and that would not qualify. So all three rungs of the ladder most likely resolve No. As of June 22 there is no restoration in the text, which leaves C1 at its deadline.

basket.reason: The deadline is the as-of date itself, and the rules describe the model as still suspended ten days after the directive.
Four more days is not enough to reverse a federal directive and also get a fully public relaunch announced.
Nineteen days after a government-ordered suspension is still short. A negotiated restoration would probably begin with closed or private access, which does not qualify.

failure_narrative: The directive turns out to be narrow and procedural, such as a short safety review or a notification requirement under an executive order or Commerce/BIS rule. Anthropic meets it quickly by adding safeguards or classifier filters, or the administration reverses course after pressure from industry, investors or allies. A court could also grant a TRO or preliminary injunction against the directive. Anthropic then puts 'Claude Fable 5' or 'Claude Mythos' back on claude.ai and the API for all US users before June 26 or July 1. It might also relabel the same model and confirm it is the same weights, which would still count. Any of these makes C2 and/or C3 resolve Yes.
hedge_thesis: A fast restoration would mean the US government's hold over frontier AI releases is weak or easy to negotiate. That would lower perceived regulatory risk for the whole frontier-AI sector. The worlds where the primary fails are the ones where the directive is dropped or blocked quickly: a court injunction, White House or Commerce backtracking, or a fast compliance deal. In those same worlds, the equity and prediction-market instruments linked to AI deregulation should reprice upward. That means Anthropic's big backers and compute suppliers (Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia), competitor labs (OpenAI) facing smaller release risk, and markets on federal AI rules or executive orders getting weakened or struck down. The reason is shared: the same political or legal result that lifts the directive also lowers the expected cost of government intervention for every frontier model release.
